e273.text: You focus your mind for 1 minute and spend 3 cursed energy. You ask a single question concerning a specific goal, event, or activity to occur within 7 days. The DM offers a truthful reply. The answer doesn’t take into account any possible circumstances that might change the outcome, such as additional glimpses of the future or the loss or gain of a companion.

e274.name: Beginner’s Luck
e274.text: You have learned to more efficiently store up luck. You can now store an additional number of Miracles equal to your CE modifier.

e274.name: Blessing of Fortune
e274.text: When you or a creature you can see fails a death saving throw, you can spend 1 Miracle and 1 CE as a reaction. The roll is now considered a natural 20. You cannot experience a breakthrough or gain a Miracle in this way.

e274.name: Innate Luck
e274.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Fated for Fortune
e274.text: Some have asked you: “Are you lucky because you have miracles by your side, or do you have miracles by your side because you’re lucky?” The answer was obvious, you are naturally lucky and your technique merely reflects that. You roll all dice generated by your cursed technique twice, picking the result of the higher one. Additionally, you can make a miracle die roll its maximum amount once per long rest. (Codex HOLD: the source never defines which dice are “miracle dice”; the maximum-die half is unusable until the die is defined.)

e275.name: Exploding Fighting Spirit
e275.text: You have learned to channel your passion for battle and fighting spirit into your cursed technique. When you hit a creature with Missile Fist, all creatures within 5 ft (other than you) take thunder damage equal to your CE modifier from the shockwaves. You can use this effect a number of times each turn equal to your proficiency bonus. When you hit a target with a Missile Fist, you gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls against that target. This bonus can stack and lasts until the end of your turn.

e275.name: Armored Missile Fist
e275.text: As a bonus action for 2 CE, you cover your hands in Missile Fists, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute: ● You gain a +2 bonus to AC while holding no weapons or shields. ● You can use your CE modifier for attack and damage rolls using your unarmed strikes. ● Your unarmed strikes deal your Missile Fist damage. ● The range of your unarmed strikes becomes 10 ft.

e275.name: Titan's Grasp
e275.text: As a reaction for 3 CE, when you or a creature within 30 ft would take damage, you interpose a Missile Fist, reducing the damage by your Missile Fist damage. Roll the user's current Missile Fist damage dice (Xd8 + CE modifier at the user's level) and reduce the incoming damage by the result.

e276.name: Immortal Jellyfish
e276.text: You have learned to reinforce your shikigami with cursed energy. As part of the bonus action to command Moon Dregs, you can spend cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to give Moon Dregs 5 temporary hit points per Cursed Energy spent. This increases to 10 temporary hit points per cursed energy at 11th level.

e276.name: Adorable Poison Jar
e276.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Poisonous Cursed Energy
e276.text: You have learned to refine your poisons within Moon Dregs to create powerful mixtures. You gain the following benefits: ● Moon Dregs deals an additional 1d6 poison damage on a hit. This increases to 2d6 at 6th level and 3d8 at 11th level. ● A creature grappled by Moon Dregs takes 2d4 poison damage at the beginning of their turn. This increases to 2d8 poison damage at 11th level. ● Poison can also be used as an enhancer. You gain 4 ability points you can use to increase Moon Dregs ability scores (max of 20).

e276.name: Maximum: Crippling Neurotoxin
e276.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Cleansing of Purity
e276.text: You have finally learned to amplify your poisonous cursed energy into a crippling neurotoxin that locks down nerves. When you use Poisonous Cursed Energy, you can spend 8 additional cursed energy to enhance the poison. If a creature fails their save against Noxious Poison they are stunned until the end of their next turn and poisoned for 8 hours. On a successful save, the target is poisoned for 1 minute. A creature poisoned in this way is treated as being under 3 temporary levels of exhaustion. If a creature fails the save by 5 or more, they are paralyzed until the end of their next turn and poisoned for 24 hours. This poison ignores cursed techniques that grant resistance, immunity, or other reductions to poison damage and the poisoned condition. This poison cannot be removed by cursed techniques or reverse cursed technique.

e277.name: Dull Pain
e277.text: A creature under the effects of Pain Killer now gains additional temporary hit points equal to 5 times your proficiency bonus. This bonus THP stacks with the base THP as a single application of the effect (it is one instance of Pain Killer granting a larger total, not two THP sources).

e277.name: Long Lasting Medicine
e277.text: A creature now gains the benefits of Pain Killer for 24 hours and is automatically stabilized if they are reduced to 0 hit points while under the effect. The 24-hour duration replaces the 1-hour duration for affected creatures.

e277.name: Maximum: Panacea
e277.text: As a reaction to a creature within 10 feet (including yourself) falling to 0 hit points you can spend 4 CE and cause them to instead remain at 10 hit points and gain the benefits of Pain Killer.

e278.name: Immobilized Limbs
e278.text: When you use Immobilizing Eyes, you can spend 1 additional CE as part of activating the technique concentrate your eyes on a specific part of the creature, also causing one of the following restrictions while you maintain your technique: ● Legs. The target's speed is halved. If the target tries to move more than their movement speed, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. ● Arms. The target gains an additional -3 penalty to attack rolls and cannot take object interactions. ● Torso. You reduce the target's AC by 3.

e278.name: Destructive Gaze
e278.text: As part of your bonus action while maintaining your technique on a creature, the target takes 2d8 psychic damage. This increases to 2d10 at 6th level, 4d8 at 11th level, and 6d8 at 18th level.

e278.name: Eye Drops
e278.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Reactive Eye Movement
e278.text: Through constant exposure, your eyes have become surprisingly tough. Whenever your eyes take damage, the damage is halved. When your eyes' hit points would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw for your eyes to stay at 1 hit point. If you have Reverse Cursed Technique, you automatically succeed. You can make this saving throw a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each long rest.

e279.name: Regalia Versatility
e279.text: You have learned to alter your regalia and can change it to a different type of weapon as a bonus action, including ranged weapons and shields. While your Regalia is a ranged weapon, it creates its own ammunition. While it is a shield, you gain a bonus to AC while wielding equal to the bonus to attack and damage rolls your regalia has. Your GM may also choose to allow more unique weapons.

e279.name: Celestial Raiment
e279.text: While you have your Regalia manifested, you can spend 3 CE as a bonus action to summon a hagoromo scarf around your body that lasts until your Regalia disappears. As a reaction, you can add your proficiency bonus to your AC until the beginning of your next turn, or to a saving throw you make as the silken scarf protects you from harm.

e279.name: Technique Release
e279.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Soul Bound Treasure
e279.text: You have learned a method that allows you to use your maximum output. On a hit, you can spend 2 CE to deal critical damage and the target must make a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. After the attack, your regalia breaks and must be resummoned. You can also use this on a Cursed Wave attack for 4 CE.

e280.name: Retrograde Station
e280.text: As an action while touching part of a nonliving object that was destroyed an hour ago, you can spend 2 cursed energy to entirely repair it. Any other fragments or separated parts of it disappear and any destroyed parts reform for the object. At 6th level this increases to 1 day, at 8th level this increases to 7 days, at 11th level this increases to 1 month, at 18th level this becomes 1 year and at 20th level this increases to any point in time.

e280.name: Flash Regress
e280.text: What if we just went backwards, like really fast? When you use Regression, you no longer provoke opportunity attacks during your regressing movement. Additionally, you can instead spend up to your proficiency bonus in cursed energy. If you spend more than 1 CE, you gain a +1 bonus to the DC or Cursed Energy check per Cursed Energy spent. At 11th level, you can push creatures Huge or smaller out of your path.

e280.name: Maximum: Sword of Retrograde
e280.text: When you use Invert Causality, your guaranteed attack deals critical damage (cannot roll black flash) and the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they are stunned until the end of your next turn.

e281.name: Musical Climax
e281.text: You've learned that just playing isn't enough, you need to build up to the best part. As an action you can start playing your instrument to charge up your technique. You can charge your technique using your action this way for a number of times equal to your CE modifier while concentrating, after which you must release your technique. You can use your reaction to launch either a Sound Blast or Sound Wave at any time while playing this way and add 2 damage die per action you use to play before releasing and ignore resistances. (The printed prerequisite names "Sound Waves"; corrected to Resonating Music as a transcription error.)

e281.name: Emotional Melodies
e281.text: As a bonus action for 5 cursed energy, you can introduce a vibe of your choice for 1 minute while concentrating. You can only have one Vibe active at a time. Deafened creatures automatically succeed. Happy Vibes: on a hit with your Sound Blast, the target makes a Charisma saving throw or be Charmed and only hear you and your music until the Vibe ends; they can repeat the save at the beginning of their turn. Sad Vibes: on a hit with your Sound Blast, the target makes a Charisma saving throw or fall prone and their speed becomes 0 until the Vibe ends; they can repeat the save at the beginning of their turn. Angry Vibes: on a hit with your Sound Blast, the target makes a Charisma saving throw or becomes berserk until the Vibe ends — a berserk creature uses their reaction to make a melee attack at the closest creature at the start of their turn and must use their action to attack; they can repeat the save at the beginning of their turn.

e281.name: Rock Squad
e281.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Maximum: Epic Solo
e281.text: Looks like the band is getting back together! An epic guitar solo is always welcome, but people came for a show. When an allied creature ends their turn within 15 feet of you during your Epic Solo, their next attack or technique deals additional d4s in thunder damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

e282.name: Piercing Burst
e282.text: You have perfected your accuracy and combined it with your piercing ability. When you use Piercing Schrift, you can also target additional targets up to your proficiency bonus that are either in front of or behind your target as long as they are within the path of the attack. You use the attack roll against the original target to determine if you would hit the additional targets.

e282.name: Cursed Seal Expert
e282.text: Through diligent practice and creativity, you have created new types of cursed seals. You gain the following options: Blinding Mark: As a bonus action for 3 CE, you mark a creature within 30 feet for 1 minute. On a hit, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they are blinded for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the save at the end of their turn, removing the blinded condition on a success. Crippling Mark: As a bonus action for 3 CE, you mark a creature within 30 feet for 1 minute. On a hit, the target must make a Constitution saving throw or have either their movement speed halved for 1 minute or disadvantage on attacks for 1 minute (your choice). A creature can repeat the save at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success.

e283.name: Shadow User
e283.text: You have furthered the uses of your shadow choosing one of the following features (This feat can be taken multiple times). Shadow Skulker: As an action for 2 CE you physically enter the shadows gaining full cover for X rounds or until you exit from a shadow within 10 feet. As an action while the technique is active, you can move into a shadow within 10 ft. You can hear and see through the shadow you entered. If the shadow is sufficiently illuminated, you exit the shadow. (X = CE mod). Shadow Envoy: As an action for 2 cursed energy, you can imbue your cursed energy into a creature's shadow within 5 ft. To attempt this technique without them noticing, you must make a Cursed Energy check against their passive perception. You can imbue conditions for when the technique is triggered. You can choose to leave either a melee attack with a range of 10 ft using Shadow Strike or a simple message. If you choose to leave a Shadow Strike, it targets a specific creature under a condition you set, uses your Cursed Energy modifier and is made at advantage if the target is unaware. If you choose a message, you can choose to leave five words. When you create the message, you can choose any number of creatures who can see the message in the shadow. Two shadow spells below 5th level. The CE cost equals the spell's level.

e283.name: Improved Bindings
e283.text: You have improved your technique and can cause shadows to physically wrap around the target, giving you the following additional effects when you use your technique: A creature must spend an attack to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check to remove the weapon. The target is treated as having two levels of exhaustion. The target must make a Constitution saving throw at the end of their turn or be stunned until the beginning of their next turn.

e284.name: Domineering Shikigami
e284.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Minor Star Shikigami
e284.text: You have learned that strengthening cursed energy lets you summon stronger shikigami. Your Minor Star Shikigami gain the following benefits. The Shikigami's Bite attack increases to 1d6. It becomes 1d8 at 6th level and 1d10 at 11th level. The Shikigami gains a +2 bonus to their Dexterity score and again at 6th, and 11th level (max of 20). When the shikigami is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

e284.name: Tyrant Shikigami
e284.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Major Star Shikigami
e284.text: You have learned that strengthening cursed energy lets you summon stronger shikigami. You can spend 1 additional cursed energy when you summon your Major Star Shikigami to increase its size category to Large. This increases to 2 cursed energy to make it Huge at 11th level and 4 cursed energy to make it Gargantuan at 18th level. For every size category larger than medium, it gains the following: +4 bonus to Strength score; +1d8 damage to Bite attacks; +30 hit points.

e284.name: Judicial Amputation
e284.prereq: Prerequisites: Must have Army of the Dictator
e284.text: If a creature fails their saving throw against your pseudo-domain by 5 or more, the damage is treated as having the Limb Removing Effect and targets one of their arms or legs.

e285.name: Enduring Shikigami
e285.text: You have learned to remove the time limit of your shikigami. Your fox shikigami (other than Inari) last until reduced to 0 hit points and you can add your proficiency bonus to any saving throws your shikigami make. You are still limited by the number of shikigami you can have active at once.

e285.name: Fox Fire
e285.text: You can create incredibly dense fog that can be triggered to erupt in a vapor explosion. For an additional 3 CE when you create an area of Cursed Fog, you make the fog incredibly thick. As an action, you can cause the fog to detonate in a vapor explosion. All creatures within the fog other than yourself must make a Constitution saving throw, taking twice your Cursed Energy modifier in d8s of cold damage or half as much damage on a success as a blue explosion rips through, igniting the fog.

e286.name: Tools of the Craft
e286.text: You can imbue a set of tools with your cursed energy, such as artisan's tools or thieve's tools. You can use your CE modifier for ability checks made using these tools and gain a +1 bonus for each CE spent on the imbuement up to a maximum of your CE modifier.

e286.name: Eyes in the Skies
e286.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Floating Tool Improvement
e286.text: When you are riding your Floating Tool, you gain a +5 bonus to your passive Perception and Investigation and can use your CE modifier for Dexterity saving throws.

e287.name: Cannibalism
e287.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Hunger of the Accursed
e287.text: Your hunger has overwhelmed your humanity and led you to resort to this inhumane act. You can now devour the corpses of human races and use them for your innate technique features. You can take a Class Feature or Innate Technique feature using the rules of Hunger of the Accursed from a dead humanoid, changing parts of your appearance to resemble them when used. You cannot take Domain Expansions using this feature. When you steal a cursed technique or innate technique feature from a dead humanoid, you can only take it if you are of the correct level and fulfill any prerequisites for using it. Additionally, you can only spend the base cost the technique requires. No matter what you copy, you can only use the technique in its base form. For example, a maximum output hollow purple would only come as a hollow purple. This changes if used with the Output option of Digestion at 6th level. Table consent: devouring a sapient humanoid corpse requires the table's consent, and for a PC corpse, that player's out-of-character consent — without it the corpse is inedible.

e287.name: Necrophage
e287.text: You have learned to more accurately extract the cursed energy from a corpse that is required for your technique. You can now devour a corpse as an action for 3 cursed energy that has been dead for a number of days equal to your Cursed Energy modifier and still have it usable for your technique if the creature's CR equals your level. This increases to twice your Cursed Energy modifier at 11th level and three times at 18th level. Necrophage's "CR equals your level" is exact-match only — a CR 5 corpse at level 6 is ineligible.

e287.name: Gourmand
e287.prereq: Prerequisite: Must have Body of the Devourer
e287.text: You have learned to appreciate the good food you have eaten. When you use Regurgitation, you gain temporary hit points equal to half the hit points of the creature whose devoured ability you are calling upon.

e288.name: Perfected Teleport
e288.text: You're grown more efficient with your teleports and have perfected their usage. The cost to use your technique instead becomes 1 CE and the cost to cast Teleport is reduced by your CE modifier. The flat cost reduction applies after adopted Maximum Output rules and does not stack with Output cost logic.

e288.name: Unlimited Marking Works
e288.text: You have learned a trick to empower your marks. You can now have a number of marks equal to five times your CE modifier. Additionally, your marks last indefinitely.

e291.name: Blood Iron
e291.text: Once per long rest, you may Polarize the iron in a living creature's blood. One Attract, Repel, or Crush ignores the metal requirement entirely and works on any creature; the target has disadvantage on its saving throw against that effect.

e291.name: Debris Throne
e291.text: While you are flying, orbiting scrap grants you +2 AC against ranged attacks. Once per turn when a ranged attack misses you, you may use your reaction to fling a shard — make a ranged technique attack against the attacker, dealing 2d8 + your CE modifier piercing damage on a hit.

e291.name: Polarity Reversal
e291.text: When a creature succeeds on its saving throw against your Attract or Repel, you may reverse the field as part of the same effect: it moves 10 feet in the opposite direction (no saving throw). You may do this once per turn.

e291.name: Polar Cage
e291.text: When Crush restrains a target, you may spend 1 additional CE to shape its metal into a cage: the restraint lasts 1 minute instead of until the end of its next turn (the target repeats the Strength save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success).

e292.name: Reed's Calculus
e292.text: The genius is the second power. As a bonus action, analyze a creature you can see: you learn its damage resistances, vulnerabilities, and immunities (if any), and the first attack each of your allies makes against it before the start of your next turn has advantage. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

e292.name: Living Bridge
e292.text: You may shape your body into a 20-ft bridge, raft, or ramp that supports up to 2,000 lb — allies cross gaps, pits, and water on your back. Alternatively, you may become a trampoline: allies who fall onto you take no falling damage and may bounce up to 20 ft as part of their movement without provoking opportunity attacks.

e292.name: Snapback
e292.text: When a creature escapes your grapple or restraint, you may use your reaction: the limb snaps back — the escapee takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage, and you may immediately make a grapple attempt against it as part of the same reaction.

e292.name: Containment Wrap
e292.text: As an action for 2 CE, envelop a Medium-or-smaller unattended object or a 10-ft cube of hazardous terrain (fire, caltrops, a swarm, a triggered trap): its effects are suppressed for 1 minute (Focus) while wrapped — flames smother, traps cannot trigger, swarms cannot leave.

e292.name: Elastic Rebound
e292.text: When a ranged attack targets you, you may use your reaction and spend 2 CE to stretch a catching membrane: reduce the attack's damage by your proficiency bonus + your CE modifier as the rubber gives. If this reduces the damage to 0, you catch the projectile — fling it back as part of the same reaction by making a ranged technique attack against a creature within 60 ft; on a hit it takes the caught attack's original damage.
